transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I hope I'm not wasting your time, I'm probably just making a bigger deal out of this than I should, but... well, I drive a taxi right now. And lately, even when I know for a fact I did my safety check on the cab—which I always do, I promise I'm a really good employee—this thought just keeps hitting me that maybe I missed something. 

And then I start worrying that somebody could get hurt, or my boss will say I lied about checking it. It's probably normal to worry a little bit about your job, right? But I just... I can't seem to make the thought shut up while I'm driving or when I'm trying to study. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Can you tell me more about how often these worries come up and if they're hard for you to control or push away when you're having them?

Um, well, like I was saying, it's... I guess it happens pretty much every day. I really try to push the thoughts away, I swear I do. I don't want to be distracted, and I want to do a good job. But even when I know for an absolute fact I did the safety check, the worry just creeps right back in. 

I'll be driving a passenger, or I'll be sitting at home trying to study for my classes, and suddenly I'm just terrified that I missed something and someone's gonna get hurt, or my boss is gonna think I lied on my sheet. I try so hard to tell myself to just stop thinking about it, but... I just can't seem to make it shut up. It just loops. I hope that doesn't make me sound crazy, or like a bad driver? I'm really careful, I promise. I just can't always control the worrying part. Does... does that answer your question okay?

When these worries come up, do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly—like checking things over and over, counting, or going through specific steps in your head—to try to calm the anxiety or make sure everything is safe?

Um... well... yeah, I guess I do have a bit of a routine. I mean, I just really want to be safe, you know? I want to do a good job. So before I can take a ride, I'll go around the car and check the tires, the lights, the doors, the meter... and make sure all my paperwork is right. Which is a good thing to do, right? Being thorough? 

But... um... I guess maybe I do it a little too much. Like, I'll check them over and over. And if something just doesn't feel right, I'll completely restart the whole check from the beginning. I even started taking pictures of everything on my phone, just so I can look at them and prove to myself I actually did it. 

I know it probably sounds a bit much... and I feel really awful about it because sometimes I'm out there doing it when passengers are actually waiting for me, and it makes me late. I really try not to inconvenience anyone, I promise, I just want to be absolutely sure everything is safe for them. Is... is that the kind of thing you meant? I hope I'm answering this right.
